title: Design System: Open Voice — Catálogo de fábrica

phase-transcribing.note: Microphone capturing. 5.27:1 on ground, 4.37:1 on panel — check the surface under it.

phase-thinking.note: Model streaming, no audio yet. Also the active-entry border and the focus outline.

phase-speaking.note: Synthesized audio playing. The warmest and quietest code in the set.

phase-idle.note: Nothing is happening. Desaturated so idleness reads as absence of signal.

phase-cut.note: Reserved for an interruption or a stopped playback. Never decoration.

display.purpose: The product name, once, in the header. Never reused as a section heading.

readout.purpose: The current entry's FAC number at 5rem. The world's real headline.

body.purpose: Document default, the header subtitle, and the composer text input.

label.purpose: Uppercase system caps: language mark, column heading, panel headings, Send.

caption.purpose: Instrumentation terms and panel status text. Read, not engraved — never uppercase.

preview.purpose: The truncated entry preview in the index.

composer-control.purpose: Mono, uppercase, 0.08em tracking. Every composer button label.

mono-number.purpose: Every latency value and the FAC column, with tabular figures so columns align.

motion.name: ease-signal
motion.purpose: The catalog index and composer controls: 160ms on color and border-color. A signal settling, not a bounce.

motion.name: ease-surface
motion.purpose: 200ms on background-color and color for hover fills.

motion.name: plot-signal
motion.purpose: The plot samples real microphone RMS every 16ms (~60fps). The sweep advances by 0.004 + level*0.09 radians per sample, so shape encodes amplitude rather than a constant rotation.

motion.name: motion-off
motion.purpose: Cancels the animation frame entirely and stops sampling. The plot keeps its static hairline grid only.

components.name: Send Button
components.description: The composer submit control. The only filled-inverted button in the system; on hover it loses the fill rather than brightening.
components.css: .ds-btn-submit { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); color: #000000; border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-submit:hover:not(:disabled), .ds-btn-submit:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 10%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-btn-submit:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-submit:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Message Field
components.description: The required text path. Square, on the panel ground, with the selection and caret pulled into the palette.

components.name: Agent Presence Plot
components.description: The signature component: a one-pixel hairline radar plot drawn from real microphone RMS. When there is no signal it rests at the baseline and draws nothing. Use the live app to see it move — this snapshot is the resting state.
components.css: .ds-plot { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; background-color: #000000; overflow: hidden; } .ds-plot canvas { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; } .ds-plot-label { position: absolute; left: 1.5rem; bottom: 1.5rem; font-family: Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: hsl(0, 0%, 70%); }

narrative.overview:
This world treats a conversation as a numbered factory catalog. Every turn is an entry with a FAC number; the agent's presence is not a widget in a corner but the work area itself, drawn as a hairline radar plot from real microphone amplitude. State is spoken in an industrial color code rather than in words, and system text is engraved into the page as tracked capitals. The ground is matte black and the plot ink is one pixel wide, so most of the screen is deliberately unprinted. The design is dense rather than explanatory: the user already knows the product, and the interface's job is to prove what just happened, measured.

Two category defaults are refused. There are no chat bubbles and no round microphone button — an answer is the entry under the current number, not a speech balloon. And there is no neon sci-fi HUD: nothing glows, nothing is translucent, nothing casts a shadow. Depth is a two-step tonal floor between black and a very dark gray panel. The interface is a sheet of plotted paper, not a head-up display.
keyCharacteristics: Matte black ground with one hairline of plot ink; the emptiness is the composition.
One colour per product state, with red reserved exclusively for an interruption.
Engraved tracked capitals for every system word; tabular monospace for every number.
Zero corner radius on any control, panel, strip or readout.
The plot is driven by real amplitude and rests at the baseline when there is no signal to read.
Depth is tonal (two steps), never shadow, blur or translucency.
An interruption is permanent: the entry is struck and stays struck in the index.

rules.name: The One Colour Per State Rule
rules.body: Every product state owns exactly one colour, and the same colour must never mean two things. A new state means a new token, not a second use of an existing one. The strip in the right rail is the only place the current phase's colour appears as a large fill.

rules.name: The Red Is Not A Button Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for a cut. A cut is a fact about the conversation, so it is permanent: the entry is struck through with a one-pixel red line, the FAC turns red, and both stay struck for the life of the session. Nothing transient, decorative, or merely loud may be red.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Lines are one physical pixel and --color-border. Thickness is not a way to express importance; position and colour are.

rules.name: The Engraved Rule
rules.body: System text is uppercase with wide tracking (0.05em for Archivo labels, 0.08em for monospace control labels). Sentence case is reserved for content that came from speech or from the user.

rules.name: The Numbering Rule
rules.body: Every number is set in Azeret Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, and FAC numbers are zero-padded to three digits (007, not 7) so the column does not reflow as the catalog grows. Never style a numeral in the display face.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Nothing hovers above the page until the pointer or the state asks for it, and even then the change is a fill, not a shadow. If a new surface needs to read as raised, add a tone or a hairline — never a shadow.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two ground values in the interface: #000000 for the field and the shell, hsl(0, 0%, 10%) for panels. A third background tone is a new design decision, not an implementation detail.

dos: Do give a product state exactly one colour and carry it on the colour-code strip, then let the label do the explaining.
Do reserve Cut Red for an interruption or an open microphone, and keep the strike permanent once a turn has been cut.
Do set every number in Azeret Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, zero-padded to three digits for FAC numbers.
Do write system text in uppercase with wide tracking (0.05em Archivo, 0.08em monospace), and reserve sentence case for words the user or the agent said.
Do let the plot rest at the baseline when there is no real signal, and drive its sweep from amplitude rather than from a clock.
Do separate regions with a one-pixel --color-border line and the two ground tones.
Do show an em dash for an unmeasured value instead of a zero or a spinner.
Do show only the states the backend can actually produce: idle, transcribing, thinking, speaking, and cut. The product must never imply a capability the backend lacks.
donts: Don't add corner radius to anything. The only rounded thing in the system is the browser's scrollbar thumb.
Don't add a shadow, a glow, a gradient, a blur or a translucent overlay to express depth, hover, focus or importance.
Don't reuse a state colour for a second meaning, or reach for a phase colour as decoration or as a large fill outside the one-pixel or 4px marks it belongs in.
Don't use red for anything that is not a cut or an open microphone — not errors in general, not hover, not emphasis.
Don't animate the plot from a constant rotation, a random walk, or a synthetic waveform. If there is no signal, the field stays flat.
Don't render the conversation as chat bubbles, or the microphone as a round button. An answer is the entry under the current FAC number.
Don't turn instrumentation into a modal, a drawer, or something the user has to ask for.
Don't translate. The language mark names the answering voice; the product does not translate.
Don't take a system face for the display voice or the numerals. Both faces are self-hosted woff2 files, and the numerals must stay tabular in every readout.
